newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - Gasoline may start leading.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - Gasoline may start leading.

text.p: Gasoline may assume its seasonal role as leader of the barrel this week and start driving the market, but Asian interest for some of the other products will also be important after crude fell to nine-month lows on Friday.

Traders said gasoline should edge higher after recent lows while gas oil should be underpinned by arbitrage opportunities to Asia. Naphtha's eastern window may come under pressure as Asian prices ease, while fuel oil is overshadowed by good supplies and modest interest.

Gasoline, which has so far stayed in the wings at a time when it should be moving higher, was expected to edge higher over the week, with many players viewing Friday's levels as the bottom of the recent fall. Eurograde barges traded at $191.50 and $192 fob ARA on Friday.
"I think we've seen its lowest price," said one trader. "Sellers are holding onto material on the expectation that prices will go higher."
"We need to see U.S. demand kick in," said another. "Cargoes are going but we would hope to see more. You have to shift at least 60,000 tonnes at the moment to make it worthwhile."

Naphtha was looking flat to weaker with demand from the Far East continuing to be the market's main support, although some players noted prices on the Asian market were beginning to come off as the first round of NWE cargoes arrived in the region.
Price levels for full range material stood at around $183/188 cif NWE on Friday.

Low sulphur cracked fuel oil was likely to track Brent this week, but should be resistant to excessive price losses on crude. Fundamentals will kick in with the bearish build-up of material in the second half of April in NWE.
Low sulphur straight run will continue to be weak, but more trade should be seen as sellers start to get edgy.
High sulphur fuel oil prices have borne up well, ignoring the fall in crude, but much of the talk has been notional as demand is very thin, particularly in northern Europe.

A high sulphur cargo sold from the U.K. at $80 fob on Friday for delivery to Iberia. Traders said the relatively high number reflected a desire to drive up pricing quotes to profit from big deliveries to Romania and Portugal.
Russian cargoes still trickle out and will be snapped up in the north and the Med. They should command solid premiums.
Asia still dominates the attention on many gas oil dealers in Europe. A late flurry of fixing at the tail end of last week could be repeated in the early part of this week, they said.

But traders are divided as to how long the eastward arbitrage window will stay open. Some appear content to load at the end of the month while others feel it is too risky to load past April 10-15 dates.
Premiums of Russian cargoes were expected to hold up this week around April flat to +$2 cif and to remain unchanged for FOD around the April +$2-4 cif NWE range.

Diesel saw a pick up in interest for small parcels last week and premiums were expected to hover around April IPE +$10, on the back of tightish supplies, despite pressure for easier numbers as the summer spec change nears.
